To compute the n-th Fibonacci number modulo 1000000007 efficiently, we use matrix exponentiation. This method allows us to calculate the Fibonacci number in logarithmic time, which is essential for large values of `n` up to about 1.8e19.

The Fibonacci sequence can be represented using matrix exponentiation:
$$
\begin{bmatrix}
F(n+1) \\
F(n)
\end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix}
1 & 1 \\
1 & 0
\end{bmatrix}^n
\begin{bmatrix}
1 \\
0
\end{bmatrix}
$$

We define a function to perform matrix exponentiation and another to multiply two matrices modulo 1000000007. The main function `fib_mod` will use these helper functions to compute the result efficiently.

Here is the implementation in the Omega machine's binary IR format:

```asm

09 01 0100 0000 0200 0000 0100 0000 0200 0000

0f 0200
0000 0000
```

This code defines the function `fib_mod` with one parameter `n` (u64) and returns a u32. It uses matrix exponentiation to compute the Fibonacci number efficiently, avoiding the need to compute each term sequentially. The implementation ensures that the result is computed modulo 1000000007.
